To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

C60-fullerenes and their amphiphilic analogues, C3-tris-malonate-C60 and D3-trismalonate-C60, interact with a bilayer of lipid DPPC, and that the tris-malonate derivatives have different interactions with the bilayer than the C60-fullerences alone.
(1) C60-fullerenes and their derivatives can permeate lipid bilayer and (2) C3 isomers can penetrate deeper into bilayer than C60-fullerens and D3 isomers.
C60-fullerenes and tris-malonylated fullerenes have different interaction with the bilayer and this may have important implications for their antioxidant activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of fullerenes with a lipid bilayer.
the mechanism of the interaction of fullerenes with lipid bilayers and its implications for the antioxidant effect of fullerenes.
the molecular mechanisms of interaction of C60-fullerenes with a lipid bilayer, and their implications for the antioxidant effect of fullerenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C3 fullerene isomer is the most promising for ROS scavenged activity.
C60 and C3 molecules are able to penetrate the lipid bilayer and that the bilayer is not a barrier to the diffusion of C60 and C60 derivatives.
C3 has a higher potential to be incorporated inside the lipid bilayer, which is in line with the experimental results that showed that C3 is a stronger ROS scavenger than D3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C60 and C3 have a potential to act as antioxidants in the cell membrane, while D3 has no potential to act as an antioxidant.
the amphiphilic C3 fullerene isomer can be considered as a potential drug for ROS scavenged in lipid bilayer environment.
C60-fullerens and C3-tris-malonate-fullerenes can cross the lipid bilayer and reach its interior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amphiphilicity of the fullerene derivatives is crucial for their ability to interact with the lipid bilayer.
the presence of the hydrophilic group at the fullerene surface is essential for its interaction with the lipid bilayer.
the amphiphilicity of tris-malonylated fullerenes is crucial for their ability to permeate the lipid bilayer.
